chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Abu Ja'far from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi from Isma'il ibn Sahil from Hammad ibn 'Isa from Hariz ibn 'Abdullah from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: He was asked about the Anfal (spoils of war), so he said: 'Every village whose people perish or are expelled from it is Anfal for Allah, Exalted and Glorious; half of it is distributed among the people, and half is for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family); and whatever is for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), it is for the Imam.'

key_terms.الْأَنْفَالِ: Spoils of war or public property
key_terms.لِلْإِمَامِ: For the Imam (referring to the divinely appointed leader)
key_terms.نَفْلٌ: Surplus or extra portion, specifically referring to Anfal

ai.seo_question: How is Anfal distributed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the specific mechanism of Anfal distribution, establishing that the portion designated for the Messenger of Allah is inherited by the Imam, thereby reinforcing the concept of Imamate as the successor to prophetic authority in both spiritual and material domains. It highlights the dual nature of Anfal as both communal wealth and a specific right of the Imam, a key distinction in Shia fiqh regarding public treasury management. This ruling underscores the continuity of divine guidance through the Imams, linking the governance of the community directly to the Ahl al-Bayt.
